I see there's no evaporator fan, that it uses defrost water to cool the refrigerant.  Makes it quiet, but water is not evaporating fast enough.

Fridge works normal.  Freezer is below 32 degrees, and fridge stays around 48 degrees, so it's working.  Doors seal really well.  Front of fridge is about 1/4 inch higher than back, so doors close properly.  I'm in So. California, so local humidity is low. "Fanless" evaporator coils seem to be a design flaw.  I put a drip pan on the floor for now, but this needs a fix or it will rot my floor.  Please advise!!!

review_text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] After Hurricane Beryl hit Houston, we lost power for 4 days. Deer meat somehow leaked from the freezer and... yeah, we had to replace an old Whirlpool fridge that came with the house.

As a replacement, we bought THIS exact LG fridge from BestBuy. I just confirmed the model number "LRFLC2706S."

Today, we had an 8-hour power outage. We made sure not to open the fridge nor freezer during this time, but after the power was restored, I opened the freezer and expected to find water in the ice tray and liquid ice cream. To my surprise, the ice cubes were still solid! Everything in the fridge was fine. Nothing had to be thrown out. I was extremely worried about the cost of having to replace everything in the fridge and freezer. We JUST did that last July for the hurricane. It cost us hundreds...

So, yeah. This fridge just won me over for a 5-star review. Highly recommended! I couldn't be happier. Quality matters.

review_text: We had a 5’x5’ insulated bathroom window replaced due to moisture getting between the panes. review_title: Look good and work okay once installed.
review_text:
Regarding measurements; I did exactly as they said.  They said they would cut and allow adequate tolerances (space).   I should have subtracted a half inch.  As they were cut, they fit so close that there is zero space between the shades and the sides of the window frame.  We had to take the end caps off of the top of the mid-rail to get enough clearance for the mid-rail to go up and down without friction.  

The instructions are complete but require some study to figure out. Especially difficult are the diagrams of how to mount the brackets.  I think of myself as being fairly mechanically inclined yet it took patience to get these shades properly assembled and in place.  One modification I found very helpful is that I put a thin spacer (1/16”) between the bracket and the top of the window opening. (We used the “Inside Mount” option.)  Otherwise the “top cell” (as they call it in the instructions) was very difficult to rock into place.  The spacers allowed room for the top cell rib to fit under the lip of the metal bracket more easily.   When standing on a step ladder trying to push the top cell in place with both hands “easier” is better. 

In conclusion, it worked okay and looked good when installed.  It is definitely room-darkening. However, unless you are handy with tools and have some patience I would recommend having a professional install these shades.  

Tools needed: Utility knife to open the package. Step ladder, drill, screwdrivers, tape measure, pencil, and a utility knife to open the package.

review_text: As a skeptic of the quality and durability of roller shades, I took a leap of faith with this brand and I'm so glad I did! I have two 58.5” bedroom windows: one facing east that blasts sunlight in the morning, and one facing west that becomes a magnifying glass in the afternoon. The iFit shades fit my windows perfectly and do their job of filtering the harsh rays without sacrificing any natural light (I wish I had found them sooner for the sake of my sun-damaged books and textiles). The ordering and delivery was super fast. The instructional videos/reviews made the installation sound easy, however I had learned a few things through trial and error: 1) The recommended 3/32 drill bit size to make the bracket holes is only appropriate if you're planning to use just the screws to secure the shade. If you're trying to drill through 1/4" metal window frames like me and want to use the drywall anchors provided, I suggest using a 7/32 drill bit instead. 2) The mounting brackets are extendable and have tiny lug nuts that need tightening prior to installation. 3) You better hope you have the dang thing centered as you like it, because once the shade is snapped into the brackets it cannot be shifted around. You can unsnap it and reposition of course, but trying to do that with a 58.5" unsealed shade is a frustrating feat! Besides those minor nuisances, I would definitely buy this product again.

product_name: Sticks and Stones Cordless Top Down/Bottom Up Blackout Cellular Fabric Shade 9/16 in. Single Cell 29.5 in. W x 48 in. L
review_title: Look good and work okay once installed.
review_text:
Regarding measurements; I did exactly as they said.  They said they would cut and allow adequate tolerances (space).   I should have subtracted a half inch.  As they were cut, they fit so close that there is zero space between the shades and the sides of the window frame.  We had to take the end caps off of the top of the mid-rail to get enough clearance for the mid-rail to go up and down without friction.  

The instructions are complete but require some study to figure out. Especially difficult are the diagrams of how to mount the brackets.  I think of myself as being fairly mechanically inclined yet it took patience to get these shades properly assembled and in place.  One modification I found very helpful is that I put a thin spacer (1/16”) between the bracket and the top of the window opening. (We used the “Inside Mount” option.)  Otherwise the “top cell” (as they call it in the instructions) was very difficult to rock into place.  The spacers allowed room for the top cell rib to fit under the lip of the metal bracket more easily.   When standing on a step ladder trying to push the top cell in place with both hands “easier” is better. 

In conclusion, it worked okay and looked good when installed.  It is definitely room-darkening. However, unless you are handy with tools and have some patience I would recommend having a professional install these shades.  

Tools needed: Utility knife to open the package. Step ladder, drill, screwdrivers, tape measure, pencil, and a utility knife to open the package.

review_text: We had a 5’x5’ insulated bathroom window replaced due to moisture getting between the panes. review_title: Very comparable to Bali and Home Decorators
review_text:

If you inset the blinds you can take the end caps off to gain maybe 1/4" of space (that’s what we did).

review_title: Poor Quality, No repair-ability, Poor warranty.
review_text: We purchased these in June of 2022 during a remodel. The blinds were professionally installed and functioned for less than 2years. We have Bali Blinds and figured we'd try these in a new room to save some $$$, and we're glad we did. I was expecting a big drop off in quality since the price is about 1/3rd of Bali, but I'm not seeing it yet. The blinds install the same way and feel good going up and down.
Only design drawback is that when inset the blinds leave a little ¼” light gap at the top that Bali blinds don't. The other obvious thing is that the widths, lengths, and colors are more limited than with high end blinds. If you inset the blinds you can take the end caps off to gain maybe 1/4" of space (that’s what we did).

review_title: Up-Down construction is weak and top sags
review_text:
We brought the up-down Chicology blackout cordless cellular shades for our 70-inch and 52-inch wide windows. They were shipped to the house, correct width and easy to installed. The blackout feature worked well. Unfortunately, the cellular top and bottom beams are all plastic; which started to sag in the middle after a week or so. Now, the top of the cellular shade has a 1/8" gap (with the window top mount beam) at the center that lets in sunlight. We then looked at a more expensive brand (Bali) and noticed magnets at the top to keep the shade top flush (close tightly) with the top mount beam when the shades are closed and all the way up. These shades did not have magnets.

Bottomline: Do not buy Chicology up-down shades if you have windows wider than 40-inches. The plastic frame top beam is weak and will sag. For wider windows, just their down-only shades would be fine.

review_title: Look good and work okay once installed.
review_text:
Regarding measurements; I did exactly as they said.  They said they would cut and allow adequate tolerances (space).   I should have subtracted a half inch.  As they were cut, they fit so close that there is zero space between the shades and the sides of the window frame.  We had to take the end caps off of the top of the mid-rail to get enough clearance for the mid-rail to go up and down without friction.  

The instructions are complete but require some study to figure out. Especially difficult are the diagrams of how to mount the brackets.  I think of myself as being fairly mechanically inclined yet it took patience to get these shades properly assembled and in place.  One modification I found very helpful is that I put a thin spacer (1/16”) between the bracket and the top of the window opening. (We used the “Inside Mount” option.)  Otherwise the “top cell” (as they call it in the instructions) was very difficult to rock into place.  The spacers allowed room for the top cell rib to fit under the lip of the metal bracket more easily.   When standing on a step ladder trying to push the top cell in place with both hands “easier” is better. 

In conclusion, it worked okay and looked good when installed.  It is definitely room-darkening. However, unless you are handy with tools and have some patience I would recommend having a professional install these shades.  

Tools needed: Utility knife to open the package. Step ladder, drill, screwdrivers, tape measure, pencil, and a utility knife to open the package.

review_text:
We brought the up-down Chicology blackout cordless cellular shades for our 70-inch and 52-inch wide windows. They were shipped to the house, correct width and easy to installed. The blackout feature worked well. Unfortunately, the cellular top and bottom beams are all plastic; which started to sag in the middle after a week or so. Now, the top of the cellular shade has a 1/8" gap (with the window top mount beam) at the center that lets in sunlight. We then looked at a more expensive brand (Bali) and noticed magnets at the top to keep the shade top flush (close tightly) with the top mount beam when the shades are closed and all the way up. These shades did not have magnets.

Bottomline: Do not buy Chicology up-down shades if you have windows wider than 40-inches. The plastic frame top beam is weak and will sag. For wider windows, just their down-only shades would be fine.

review_title: Look good and work okay once installed.
review_text:
Regarding measurements; I did exactly as they said.  They said they would cut and allow adequate tolerances (space).   I should have subtracted a half inch.  As they were cut, they fit so close that there is zero space between the shades and the sides of the window frame.  We had to take the end caps off of the top of the mid-rail to get enough clearance for the mid-rail to go up and down without friction.  

The instructions are complete but require some study to figure out. Especially difficult are the diagrams of how to mount the brackets.  I think of myself as being fairly mechanically inclined yet it took patience to get these shades properly assembled and in place.  One modification I found very helpful is that I put a thin spacer (1/16”) between the bracket and the top of the window opening. (We used the “Inside Mount” option.)  Otherwise the “top cell” (as they call it in the instructions) was very difficult to rock into place.  The spacers allowed room for the top cell rib to fit under the lip of the metal bracket more easily.   When standing on a step ladder trying to push the top cell in place with both hands “easier” is better. 

In conclusion, it worked okay and looked good when installed.  It is definitely room-darkening. However, unless you are handy with tools and have some patience I would recommend having a professional install these shades.  

Tools needed: Utility knife to open the package. Step ladder, drill, screwdrivers, tape measure, pencil, and a utility knife to open the package.

review_text: As a skeptic of the quality and durability of roller shades, I took a leap of faith with this brand and I'm so glad I did! I have two 58.5” bedroom windows: one facing east that blasts sunlight in the morning, and one facing west that becomes a magnifying glass in the afternoon. The iFit shades fit my windows perfectly and do their job of filtering the harsh rays without sacrificing any natural light (I wish I had found them sooner for the sake of my sun-damaged books and textiles). The ordering and delivery was super fast. The instructional videos/reviews made the installation sound easy, however I had learned a few things through trial and error: 1) The recommended 3/32 drill bit size to make the bracket holes is only appropriate if you're planning to use just the screws to secure the shade. If you're trying to drill through 1/4" metal window frames like me and want to use the drywall anchors provided, I suggest using a 7/32 drill bit instead. 2) The mounting brackets are extendable and have tiny lug nuts that need tightening prior to installation. 3) You better hope you have the dang thing centered as you like it, because once the shade is snapped into the brackets it cannot be shifted around. You can unsnap it and reposition of course, but trying to do that with a 58.5" unsealed shade is a frustrating feat! Besides those minor nuisances, I would definitely buy this product again.

product_name: Antique Pewter Cordless Top Down Bottom Up Blackout 9/16 in. Single Cell Cellular Fabric Shade 44 in. W x 72 in. L
review_title: Look good and work okay once installed.
review_text:
Regarding measurements; I did exactly as they said.  They said they would cut and allow adequate tolerances (space).   I should have subtracted a half inch.  As they were cut, they fit so close that there is zero space between the shades and the sides of the window frame.  We had to take the end caps off of the top of the mid-rail to get enough clearance for the mid-rail to go up and down without friction.  

The instructions are complete but require some study to figure out. Especially difficult are the diagrams of how to mount the brackets.  I think of myself as being fairly mechanically inclined yet it took patience to get these shades properly assembled and in place.  One modification I found very helpful is that I put a thin spacer (1/16”) between the bracket and the top of the window opening. (We used the “Inside Mount” option.)  Otherwise the “top cell” (as they call it in the instructions) was very difficult to rock into place.  The spacers allowed room for the top cell rib to fit under the lip of the metal bracket more easily.   When standing on a step ladder trying to push the top cell in place with both hands “easier” is better. 

In conclusion, it worked okay and looked good when installed.  It is definitely room-darkening. However, unless you are handy with tools and have some patience I would recommend having a professional install these shades.  

Tools needed: Utility knife to open the package. Step ladder, drill, screwdrivers, tape measure, pencil, and a utility knife to open the package.

review_title: The Alpine Brand, Spiral Multi-Function Christmas Tree w/ Multi-Color LED Light is an easy to set...
review_text: The Alpine Brand, Spiral Multi-Function Christmas Tree w/ Multi-Color LED Light is an easy to setup colorful Christmas tree for home or yard decoration. I selected this tree for my wife who has been wishing to add a lighted Christmas tree in our yard to go with our other decorations. Due to its spiral design it collapses as flat as a pancake for easy storage, taking up very little space. The tree is very light weight in design, consisting primarily of a single rope light attached to a plastic spiral guide by many small plastic ties. The light weight plastic rope light spirals up where it wraps around the star at the top and spirals back down forming two spirals to form the shape of the tree. Monofilament fishing line is tied from each spiral to the one below such that the weight of the rope light spacing is kept even all the way from top to bottom. The base and three section center support pole are made of light gauge painted steel. As I tired to assemble the tree, it appeared to be assembled incorrectly at the factory as I was unable to attach the star to the pole at the top due to the rope light being too far from the pole center. See photos. I managed a work around by placing a small cut in the top plastic hanger to slip the rope light thought to get the rope light close enough to the center to attach the star to the top of the pole. I would have had to disable the entire tree to correctly thread the rope light in my opinion. The monofilament fishing line makes for invisible support for the lighted tree spirals; however, I question the durability of the line exposed to sunlight, cold temperatures and the forces of wind outdoors. I though the quality of this tree could have been better, both in materials and factory assembly, to include the printed instructions for assembly. The painted steel parts seemed somewhat flimsy to me. And by placing the one small cut (modification) I made to assemble the tree, could void the warranty.

review_text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I like that these planters come in a set of two because it makes it easier to style and find a place to put them. I much prefer a set of two identical planters like these over different size sets which are fun in theory but not as easy to use. Although these planters are narrower on the bottom than the top,  the difference is slight enough that they won’t tip over or be unsteady. I have experienced many badly proportioned planters that have tipped over due to wind and other outdoor elements in the garden. The textured brown design doesn’t make them the most aesthetic or ornamental planters but this also helps them blend in more with the surroundings and allow the plants to shine. There is a removable plug on the bottom so there is a drainage hole if you plant directly into the planter outside. I like that this is versatile and doesn’t require drilling if you want to use it outside but you can also plug it back up if you don’t need the hole. It is unclear why the bottom is printed with “for outdoor use drill hole here” with an arrow pointed at the already existing hole but just know that no drilling is required if one hole is sufficient for your needs. 

They were a lot more lightweight than I expected. They basically feel like plastic (or resin) and there is some off gassing and chemical scent. I am not opposed to the weight as it makes the planters easier to move around. I also have less fear that they will crack and break from accidentally tipping over or falling. I do wonder how long they will last in sunlight. If you are looking for lightweight planters that look like natural neutral stone, these would be a good choice to consider.

review_text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I didn’t know what to expect when I received this Alpine Corporation pond fogger, but as someone who loves to fiddle with making my outdoor fish pond better and better, I was excited to try it.  And let me tell you, this is an awesome addition to my pond, and I absolutely love it!
 
The fogger came well packaged and in perfect condition.  There isn’t much to put together…there is the lighted fogger, and it sits down in a floating ring.  After attaching the cord, the cord to a power brick, and then to an outlet, you are ready to go.
 
I was shocked at how quickly the fog started…it is pretty much immediate.  So you don’t need it to warm up the device, which is fantastic if you have excited kids waiting to watch.  The fog is thick and billowing, and very fun to watch.  
 
The lights are bright, though the effect of obviously more interesting at dusk or night.  I consider this effect more of a bonus, as the fog is the absolute star of the show.  
 
My pond is relatively shallow, so I wondered if that might hamper the output, but that certainly doesn’t seem to be the case…I certainly didn’t expect it to work as well as it did.
 
One thing I really appreciate is that the cord is very long…my outlet isn’t super close to my pond, so I love the length means I didn’t have to use an extension cord.
 
So far it’s holding up as new, but the instructions tell you how to clean and service your pond fogger, so there should be plenty of life for years to come.
 
My kids and I love this pond fogger by Alpine Corporation, and I certainly recommend it without reservation.

review_title: Beautiful birdbath for our smaller birds
review_text: [This review was collected as part of a promotion.] We love sitting in our backyard while drinking our morning coffee and in the evenings when we are enjoying cocktails. Watching the squirrels & birds that come to our feeders is entertaining & restful. I got this Mosaic Glass Birdbath from Alpine to place near the flowering vines on the back fence where a lot of smaller birds & butterflies like to hang out. The mosaic bowl has a mixture of blue colors & looks really pretty when filled with water. I did have a bit of trouble getting it to stay attached to the small suction cups that hold the bowl in place. With some repositioning of the cups, it is possible to get all 4 to grip at the same time. The legs of the stand are not very sturdy & you have to make sure it stays level so that they don’t wobble. We are going to put this birdbath in a grassy area so my husband is going to dig some small holes so that we can place the legs down into the ground & then put something heavy on them to make sure they stay put. This isn’t a deal breaker though because the birdbath is such a pretty piece & the small birds should love it. I don’t think we would have the wobbly leg issues if we were going to put the birdbath on a patio or anything else that is a hard surface.

review_text:

I purchased one last year and happened to get a defective one. I decided to make it a DYI project out of it, and here are the highlights of what I did: (YouTube video coming soon)

I purchased 3 cans of Rust Oleum Painter's Touch 2X Multipurpose Paint, 12 Oz cans.
One was purple, the other 2 were black. 
Unbent the top metal feathers to their appropriate positions.
Dislodged some of the metal feathers outwards on the body. 
Soldered the tips where the metal ends by the tail.
Spray-painted the back of the tail feathers initially with purple, followed by black.
Re-secured the fastening metal bracket to keep the tail in place.
Enhanced the colors with DecoArt Metallic paints.
Applied the glow paint to the tips of the tail feathers for a special effect.
I then carefully wrapped the peacock with solar white lights.
All products I used were from Home depot, with the exception of the solar lights and probably the glow paint.

review_title: The Alpine Silver Christmas Tree Décor with Cool White LED Lights arrived in satisfactory time af...
review_text: The Alpine Silver Christmas Tree Décor with Cool White LED Lights arrived in satisfactory time after ordering. It was packed well but was also easy to open from the 2 boxes. Included with the tree was a plate for the tree to be secured to with an eye bolt. Now if I want to use this tree outside for the holidays, included are 4 stakes to hold down the plate onto the ground, that is if the ground isn't too frozen in December in Southern Wisconsin for such a feat. I think it might look nice as an accent tree in my outdoor holiday display. Having a 16 foot long power cord for the tree certainly helps with easily reaching an extension cord holding plugs of my other holiday decorations. It might even be nice to leave outside all year long (white lights don't evoke Christmas to me in June) - or even on a patio or in a 4 season room. But for this review, I've kept the tree indoors. It's about 5 feet tall and what I would consider a "slim tree" so it can fit very easily into your living space, holiday time or not. Lots of people keep lit trees in their living areas year round also. I guess you could decorate the tree if you desire but its design is probably to keep it naked. The silver wrapping on the trunk and all the way up the branches to the lights does a nice job of reflecting the 184 cool white lights. The tree arrives collapsed and then you spread the branches out to shape the tree as you want. I like to keep the tree more upswept than out but then again, I don't want to keep moving, tugging, spreading, and playing with the branches. I'm not assured that the constant moving of the branches over time will not weaken the stability of the branches/lights, even with all that silver tape/wrapping. So instead of collapsing the tree holiday season after holiday season, I may just leave it spread out as I have it right now, especially with its slim footprint- it should not take up a lot of space, whether in my basement or still in my living area. Very nice addition to my home - outside, inside, holiday time, year round.

product_name: Festive Indoor/Outdoor Artificial Christmas Tree with Green LED Lights, Silver
review_text:
I starting looking for a specific kind of tree for Christmas decor. I wanted something very simple, about 60” high that was pre-lit with clear preferably white light and didn’t require adding any ornaments. It just looked good by itself. 

I found this tree made by Alpine. It met all of the criteria, was silver in color and the perfect size. I can make it as wide as I want or as narrow. It came with everything you would need if putting it outdoors but I wanted mine on the house. 

Simple to attached to stand but putting a screw hook in a hole (pre-drilled) that fits into the pole of the tree that locks it in so that if you lift it it doesn’t come off the base. Screwing that screw in was a big problem. Perhaps it wasn’t drilled properly or poorly because I had to use channel locks and every bit of strength I had to get that screw to go into the tree. Just that simple task took about 15 minutes. Because of that I took away half of a star from the 5 star rating it would have gotten. 

As the pictures show it’s a very simple tree but stunning. I will have to find something to make a tree blanket to cover up all the 15” of open space from the base to just below the lowest branches. For that I took away another half of star. 

But overall I would recommend this to a friend, the screw glitch may not happen with every tree. Aside from the screw, it’s well made and very striking. Apparently they also come in different colors and multi- color.

review_text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I like that these planters come in a set of two because it makes it easier to style and find a place to put them. I much prefer a set of two identical planters like these over different size sets which are fun in theory but not as easy to use. Although these planters are narrower on the bottom than the top,  the difference is slight enough that they won’t tip over or be unsteady. I have experienced many badly proportioned planters that have tipped over due to wind and other outdoor elements in the garden. The textured brown design doesn’t make them the most aesthetic or ornamental planters but this also helps them blend in more with the surroundings and allow the plants to shine. There is a removable plug on the bottom so there is a drainage hole if you plant directly into the planter outside. I like that this is versatile and doesn’t require drilling if you want to use it outside but you can also plug it back up if you don’t need the hole. It is unclear why the bottom is printed with “for outdoor use drill hole here” with an arrow pointed at the already existing hole but just know that no drilling is required if one hole is sufficient for your needs. 

They were a lot more lightweight than I expected. They basically feel like plastic (or resin) and there is some off gassing and chemical scent. I am not opposed to the weight as it makes the planters easier to move around. I also have less fear that they will crack and break from accidentally tipping over or falling. I do wonder how long they will last in sunlight. If you are looking for lightweight planters that look like natural neutral stone, these would be a good choice to consider.

review_title: This is a two pack of the Wasp trap lantern. What I like about the lantern is it’s a “set and for...
review_text:
This is a two pack of the Wasp trap lantern. What I like about the lantern is it’s a “set and forget” solution. There is no bait or sticky paper that needs to be replenished over time. The lantern itself is the trap. The shape of the lantern is a conical shape where it is wider at the base. The bottom has a funnel type shape leading into the lantern. Once the wasp flies in, it has a hard time getting out due to the shape of the glass. I like that this is a natural solution and that it doesn’t attract helpful bees.

On top of being a wasp trap, this is a beautiful set of lanterns. Each lantern features beautiful amber glass with a design pressed into it. The glass doesn’t have mold markings so it is a clean design with quality finishings. The top has a metal ring where the rope attaches. The rope is nice and thick and ties into nautical or even country décor. The rope is used to hang the lantern; I hung mine on a garden shepherd’s hook, but this lantern can even be set on a table.

The solar light has an on/off switch next to the panel. The light unit is removable from the top (so you can dump out any dead wasps) and nests inside the lantern where the solar panel is flush with the top of the glass. The lantern uses a single LED light which gives a beautiful glow in the evening. When fully charged from a bright day, the lantern will glow nearly all night.

review_title: The Alpine Silver Christmas Tree Décor with Cool White LED Lights arrived in satisfactory time af...
review_text: The Alpine Silver Christmas Tree Décor with Cool White LED Lights arrived in satisfactory time after ordering. It was packed well but was also easy to open from the 2 boxes. Included with the tree was a plate for the tree to be secured to with an eye bolt. Now if I want to use this tree outside for the holidays, included are 4 stakes to hold down the plate onto the ground, that is if the ground isn't too frozen in December in Southern Wisconsin for such a feat. I think it might look nice as an accent tree in my outdoor holiday display. Having a 16 foot long power cord for the tree certainly helps with easily reaching an extension cord holding plugs of my other holiday decorations. It might even be nice to leave outside all year long (white lights don't evoke Christmas to me in June) - or even on a patio or in a 4 season room. But for this review, I've kept the tree indoors. It's about 5 feet tall and what I would consider a "slim tree" so it can fit very easily into your living space, holiday time or not. Lots of people keep lit trees in their living areas year round also. I guess you could decorate the tree if you desire but its design is probably to keep it naked. The silver wrapping on the trunk and all the way up the branches to the lights does a nice job of reflecting the 184 cool white lights. The tree arrives collapsed and then you spread the branches out to shape the tree as you want. I like to keep the tree more upswept than out but then again, I don't want to keep moving, tugging, spreading, and playing with the branches. I'm not assured that the constant moving of the branches over time will not weaken the stability of the branches/lights, even with all that silver tape/wrapping. So instead of collapsing the tree holiday season after holiday season, I may just leave it spread out as I have it right now, especially with its slim footprint- it should not take up a lot of space, whether in my basement or still in my living area. Very nice addition to my home - outside, inside, holiday time, year round.

product_name: Festive Indoor/Outdoor Artificial Christmas Tree with Red LED Lights, Silver
review_text:
I starting looking for a specific kind of tree for Christmas decor. I wanted something very simple, about 60” high that was pre-lit with clear preferably white light and didn’t require adding any ornaments. It just looked good by itself. 

I found this tree made by Alpine. It met all of the criteria, was silver in color and the perfect size. I can make it as wide as I want or as narrow. It came with everything you would need if putting it outdoors but I wanted mine on the house. 

Simple to attached to stand but putting a screw hook in a hole (pre-drilled) that fits into the pole of the tree that locks it in so that if you lift it it doesn’t come off the base. Screwing that screw in was a big problem. Perhaps it wasn’t drilled properly or poorly because I had to use channel locks and every bit of strength I had to get that screw to go into the tree. Just that simple task took about 15 minutes. Because of that I took away half of a star from the 5 star rating it would have gotten. 

As the pictures show it’s a very simple tree but stunning. I will have to find something to make a tree blanket to cover up all the 15” of open space from the base to just below the lowest branches. For that I took away another half of star. 

But overall I would recommend this to a friend, the screw glitch may not happen with every tree. Aside from the screw, it’s well made and very striking. Apparently they also come in different colors and multi- color.

If using indoors, the base is a little wobbly, but could easily be secured with some sort of weight at the bottom covered by a tree skirt. The lights are well dispersed and beautiful at night. We have just had the product for a day, but I know that we will enjoy it for many nights and hopefully years to come. At a price point of up to $60 I would say this is an excellent product. At a price point beyond that I would say it is average.

review_title: The Alpine Silver Christmas Tree Décor with Cool White LED Lights arrived in satisfactory time af...
review_text: The Alpine Silver Christmas Tree Décor with Cool White LED Lights arrived in satisfactory time after ordering. It was packed well but was also easy to open from the 2 boxes. Included with the tree was a plate for the tree to be secured to with an eye bolt. Now if I want to use this tree outside for the holidays, included are 4 stakes to hold down the plate onto the ground, that is if the ground isn't too frozen in December in Southern Wisconsin for such a feat. I think it might look nice as an accent tree in my outdoor holiday display. Having a 16 foot long power cord for the tree certainly helps with easily reaching an extension cord holding plugs of my other holiday decorations. It might even be nice to leave outside all year long (white lights don't evoke Christmas to me in June) - or even on a patio or in a 4 season room. But for this review, I've kept the tree indoors. It's about 5 feet tall and what I would consider a "slim tree" so it can fit very easily into your living space, holiday time or not. Lots of people keep lit trees in their living areas year round also. I guess you could decorate the tree if you desire but its design is probably to keep it naked. The silver wrapping on the trunk and all the way up the branches to the lights does a nice job of reflecting the 184 cool white lights. The tree arrives collapsed and then you spread the branches out to shape the tree as you want. I like to keep the tree more upswept than out but then again, I don't want to keep moving, tugging, spreading, and playing with the branches. I'm not assured that the constant moving of the branches over time will not weaken the stability of the branches/lights, even with all that silver tape/wrapping. So instead of collapsing the tree holiday season after holiday season, I may just leave it spread out as I have it right now, especially with its slim footprint- it should not take up a lot of space, whether in my basement or still in my living area. Very nice addition to my home - outside, inside, holiday time, year round.

product_name: Indoor/Outdoor Artificial Christmas Tree with Cool White LED Lights, Silver
review_text:
I starting looking for a specific kind of tree for Christmas decor. I wanted something very simple, about 60” high that was pre-lit with clear preferably white light and didn’t require adding any ornaments. It just looked good by itself. 

I found this tree made by Alpine. It met all of the criteria, was silver in color and the perfect size. I can make it as wide as I want or as narrow. It came with everything you would need if putting it outdoors but I wanted mine on the house. 

Simple to attached to stand but putting a screw hook in a hole (pre-drilled) that fits into the pole of the tree that locks it in so that if you lift it it doesn’t come off the base. Screwing that screw in was a big problem. Perhaps it wasn’t drilled properly or poorly because I had to use channel locks and every bit of strength I had to get that screw to go into the tree. Just that simple task took about 15 minutes. Because of that I took away half of a star from the 5 star rating it would have gotten. 

As the pictures show it’s a very simple tree but stunning. I will have to find something to make a tree blanket to cover up all the 15” of open space from the base to just below the lowest branches. For that I took away another half of star. 

But overall I would recommend this to a friend, the screw glitch may not happen with every tree. Aside from the screw, it’s well made and very striking. Apparently they also come in different colors and multi- color.

After assembly and turning it on, the wrapping around the tree seemed more acceptable and reflected the lights nicely. The tree was easy to assemble and I appreciated the stakes for sturdy placement outside. If using indoors, the base is a little wobbly, but could easily be secured with some sort of weight at the bottom covered by a tree skirt. The branches were easy to move/shape into the desired placement and the wire throughout the branches seems to be substantial. Tree is easily reshaped for compact storage. The lights are well dispersed and beautiful at night. We have just had the product for a day, but I know that we will enjoy it for many nights and hopefully years to come. At a price point of up to $60 I would say this is an excellent product. At a price point beyond that I would say it is average.

product_name: Medium Brown Indoor/Outdoor Stone-Look Resin Squared Planter (Set of 2)
review_text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I like that these planters come in a set of two because it makes it easier to style and find a place to put them. I much prefer a set of two identical planters like these over different size sets which are fun in theory but not as easy to use. Although these planters are narrower on the bottom than the top,  the difference is slight enough that they won’t tip over or be unsteady. I have experienced many badly proportioned planters that have tipped over due to wind and other outdoor elements in the garden. The textured brown design doesn’t make them the most aesthetic or ornamental planters but this also helps them blend in more with the surroundings and allow the plants to shine. There is a removable plug on the bottom so there is a drainage hole if you plant directly into the planter outside. I like that this is versatile and doesn’t require drilling if you want to use it outside but you can also plug it back up if you don’t need the hole. It is unclear why the bottom is printed with “for outdoor use drill hole here” with an arrow pointed at the already existing hole but just know that no drilling is required if one hole is sufficient for your needs. 

They were a lot more lightweight than I expected. They basically feel like plastic (or resin) and there is some off gassing and chemical scent. I am not opposed to the weight as it makes the planters easier to move around. I also have less fear that they will crack and break from accidentally tipping over or falling. I do wonder how long they will last in sunlight. If you are looking for lightweight planters that look like natural neutral stone, these would be a good choice to consider.

review_title: The Alpine Silver Christmas Tree Décor with Cool White LED Lights arrived in satisfactory time af...
review_text: The Alpine Silver Christmas Tree Décor with Cool White LED Lights arrived in satisfactory time after ordering. It was packed well but was also easy to open from the 2 boxes. Included with the tree was a plate for the tree to be secured to with an eye bolt. Now if I want to use this tree outside for the holidays, included are 4 stakes to hold down the plate onto the ground, that is if the ground isn't too frozen in December in Southern Wisconsin for such a feat. I think it might look nice as an accent tree in my outdoor holiday display. Having a 16 foot long power cord for the tree certainly helps with easily reaching an extension cord holding plugs of my other holiday decorations. It might even be nice to leave outside all year long (white lights don't evoke Christmas to me in June) - or even on a patio or in a 4 season room. But for this review, I've kept the tree indoors. It's about 5 feet tall and what I would consider a "slim tree" so it can fit very easily into your living space, holiday time or not. Lots of people keep lit trees in their living areas year round also. I guess you could decorate the tree if you desire but its design is probably to keep it naked. The silver wrapping on the trunk and all the way up the branches to the lights does a nice job of reflecting the 184 cool white lights. The tree arrives collapsed and then you spread the branches out to shape the tree as you want. I like to keep the tree more upswept than out but then again, I don't want to keep moving, tugging, spreading, and playing with the branches. I'm not assured that the constant moving of the branches over time will not weaken the stability of the branches/lights, even with all that silver tape/wrapping. So instead of collapsing the tree holiday season after holiday season, I may just leave it spread out as I have it right now, especially with its slim footprint- it should not take up a lot of space, whether in my basement or still in my living area. Very nice addition to my home - outside, inside, holiday time, year round.

product_name: Indoor/Outdoor Artificial Christmas Tree with Multi-Colored LED Lights, Silver
review_text:
I starting looking for a specific kind of tree for Christmas decor. I wanted something very simple, about 60” high that was pre-lit with clear preferably white light and didn’t require adding any ornaments. It just looked good by itself. 

I found this tree made by Alpine. It met all of the criteria, was silver in color and the perfect size. I can make it as wide as I want or as narrow. It came with everything you would need if putting it outdoors but I wanted mine on the house. 

Simple to attached to stand but putting a screw hook in a hole (pre-drilled) that fits into the pole of the tree that locks it in so that if you lift it it doesn’t come off the base. Screwing that screw in was a big problem. Perhaps it wasn’t drilled properly or poorly because I had to use channel locks and every bit of strength I had to get that screw to go into the tree. Just that simple task took about 15 minutes. Because of that I took away half of a star from the 5 star rating it would have gotten. 

As the pictures show it’s a very simple tree but stunning. I will have to find something to make a tree blanket to cover up all the 15” of open space from the base to just below the lowest branches. For that I took away another half of star. 

But overall I would recommend this to a friend, the screw glitch may not happen with every tree. Aside from the screw, it’s well made and very striking. Apparently they also come in different colors and multi- color.

product_name: 33 in. Tall Indoor/Outdoor Metallic Peacock Standing Yard Statue Decoration, Multicolor
review_text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I live in New England and we have four seasons where our yard dramatically changes its look. We usually add yard decorations for our enjoyment and create surprise conversation pieces for our visitors. I really liked this peacock even though the colors are not natural for my landscape.  I got this in the wintertime and the ground is frozen, so the pictures aren’t going to be as good as I imagine they would be in the spring. One thing is sure, it shines brightly in the sunlight and puts a smile on my face. 

It is an all-metal frame that has stamped leaves welded to a hollow, steel frame. The main colors are metallic turquois, magenta and gold. It comes bubble wrapped in three pieces (the feet, the body/head, and the tail fan.) It was easy to assemble, the body had rods that fit into the hollow legs and secured with a painted set screw. The tail attached with two rods and hangs off the back side. The underside of the tail is painted matt black so it does not draw attention to the underside and conceals the framework with shade. It looks good from most angles. The head faces backwards so it’s natural to have the tail on display. 

The tail sits lower than the feet so, I pushed down to let the bottom feathers lay flat on the ground. When I placed it in the front garden, I grabbed a large cobble to rest on the foot loop to help it survive the winter wind. 

Even though I’m keeping it out this winter, I think I will put it away in the fall. I think I will move it around to different bushes throughout the summer just for variety. While it stands on its own, I wish they had included some lawn spikes to help further secure it. 
Overall, it is a really fun item to look at.

review_text:
Nothing beats back the doldrums of a long, frigid winter like thoughts of springtime-- sunny skies, flowers, the birds and the bees... 
And regardless of the wintery temperatures, you can capture a bit of the whimsy of spring with this delightful solar-powered bee wind mobile from Alpine Corporation.
I chose to hang my mobile near the front door as a cheery welcome to visitors. Initially, I had serious concerns its components would be able to withstand the weeks of sub-zero temps-- but those concerns weren't necessary, as this mobile's LED lights, powered by the solar cells atop, have lit up like clockwork in each of the little bees every night. And glancing outside at 2 a.m., the light element in each of those six bees are are still going strong. Amazing!
The mobile comes pre-assembled-- you simply pick a location that provides at least four-five hours of sun, turn on the switch on the underside of the solar cell, and by that evening, you'll have a pretty cascade of illuminated bees providing a pretty, serene decor.
I love this fun, unique wind mobile from Alpine-- it's a well-made product, able to withstand the elements of its surroundings for years to come. Highly recommend!

review_text:
We ordered this Alpine Corporation 27" outdoor solar powered wind mobile online, and it was packaged well and delivered on time.

This particular mobile doesn't seem that fragile, but it was packed inside of a shipping-box with some packing paper, and inside that shipping-box was the product box. Inside the product box, the mobile was packaged in foam. So great care was taken to prevent the product from damage.

The mobile is pretty big. The bees are the size of golf balls, and the longest one hangs about 27 inches from the top. All the bees hang at different lengths, and each one has a build in LED light. The base at the top has a solar charger, and there is an ON/OFF switch under the base.

While unboxing, the bees tangled up and were tricky to get untangled but while it's been hanging, they have not gotten tangled again. I'm sure given a wind storm or something like that, you may need to untangle the bees. The instructions say that this product is weather and rain resistant, so it can be used outside, but the back of the instructions say that this product is not built to withstand extreme temperatures, and that if water gets into the device and freezes they are not responsible for the damage or replacement. This makes me think that this product is only good for Spring/Summer/Fall in my northern climate.

Overall, I thought it was nice, and my wife and son like it. It's a bit pricey but not prohibitively expensive. For the price, they could have built in more weather protection for the solar charger base.

review_title: Do Not Buy - unless you feel like lugging it back to the store to return it.
review_text:
I purchased this fountain in April 2021.  I absolutely loved it after I set it up.  I did have to purchase a net bag to put around the pump.  It was so easily clogged up by the tiniest pieces of soil, leaves, etc.  However, I was still fine with that.  A couple weeks ago I noticed a paint chip on one of the leaves that the water trickles down on.  I decided to ignore that also.  Well now the paint is chipping off all over the places.  It is not acceptable for a price point over $200.  I contacted customer service.  So it is returnable, but I either have to find a box big enough to put it in and take it to UPS or bring it back to the store.  They did offer a carrier pick up, but again, would have to pack it up in a box.  That would be fine if it wasn't a huge object that I definitely do not have a box laying around for.  So off to the store I go with it.  Save yourself the headache unless you are ok with a fountain that has paint chipping off of it all over the place.  

Note - I do have this fountain outside.  It might be ok as an indoor fountain, but I believe it is the water that is chipping the paint off.  The material that is used for the top of the fountain is not made to be painted.

review_title: I've enjoyed the relaxing sight of solar-powered, color changing LED wind chimes since the first ...
review_text:
I've enjoyed the relaxing sight of solar-powered, color changing LED wind chimes since the first time I saw one; they provide a nice decorative addition and automatically turn on/off (around sunset/sunrise) ... the 28" 3D Flowers Wind Chime is no exception (Photos #1 thru #3). Except for the quality issues that I highlighted below, I love it. It did not work after charging for 24 hours per the instructions, so I opened it up to ensure the battery was properly seated and discovered some issues:
1) Photo #4 shows a wire loop that is too long and shorted against the "+" battery terminal causing it to not work. Also shown is poor quality connections which could reduce run time.
2) I expected about an 8-hour run time, but got 4-1/2 with the LEDs changing to red at 3 hours and fading with the battery discharge. Also shown in Photo #4 is a 300 mAh NiCad battery; the capacity coupled with poor connections are the likely culprits. A far less toxic and extended performance choice would be a NiMH battery.
3) The 3D flowers are about the size of tennis balls; the lower ones tend to get tangled with each other (see Photo #5). Possible remedies are lengthening the wire leads by 1/2" to 1" and/or increasing the diameter of the top to 6".

Again, I love seeing this wind chime in action, but cannot recommend it due to the quality issues.

review_title: This is great for the money. It's made of a resin-plastic material. The base is small, maybe 12-1...
review_text:
This is great for the money. It's made of a resin-plastic material. The base is small, maybe 12-14" but it WILL stand straight-up if you take the time to level the ground underneath it. It won't get knocked over by strong wind if you keep it filled with water to keep it heavy. A large dog (or small child) may still be able to knock it over, though.

It has a pleasant sound and the small motor has a few speed settings. My motor stopped working once-- but I followed the care instructions and was able to get it working again. I also buried my cord in the ground to hide it and have had no problems.

Be sure to keep it filled-up (water will splash out if you have it on a high speed, and also if there's a strong wind) and keep junk (leaves, twigs, etc.) from staying in the bowl too long...

Put it on level ground, keep it filled, and take care of it and you will enjoy it. Very good for small backyards and patios and would be really nice under a gazebo or trellis...

review_text:
New out of the box, this fountain was fine, momentarily. After several days, it started to leak in multiple places. On emptying and inspecting, I found the base to be riddled with small cracks, and the plaster separating at key areas at the base. Additionally, even though it’s never been in direct sunlight, the color finish turned to a depressing gray within months, and the filter foam became brittle and failed to properly disperse the water causing a lot of splash

Instead of returning, (huge hassle) I re-painted it, and had bought a giant barrel liner.... I cut to fit and placed the fountain into the liner with rocks and pond lights and it’s satisfactory now since it can all leak right back into itself. At least they gave me enough hose in the back to sink the pump into the base liner.

The price for the fountain doesn’t include the cost of your time and materials to force it to work the way it should, so make sure to be prepared for the extra expense.

review_title: Wow this 8 tier fountain is one piece and heavy, get someone to help you move it. Okay the label ...
review_text:
Wow this 8 tier fountain is one piece and heavy, get someone to help you move it. Okay the label says alpine manufacturing California. So I believe it is made there. It's not flimsy material It's heavy, so most companies shipping from overseas lower costs by using flimsy material, since this is heavy that's another checkmark for being made in usa. I received this some time before 11 am. Because it was sitting at my door at 11 when I checked mail. It took me until 2:15 pm to complete setup. That's why you need a helper. 
First picture shows it setup basically for testing with no water. Then I read the instructions to see about how much water it would hold.  Yup you guessed it. Had to reset it because the instructions say smooth level surface.  Had to use some lexun and place it on the peagravel then level it. Ok now plugged into the wall then plugged the LED light system in. Only do the lights.  Then pull the plastic tube out the back access door as much as possible, because You have to turn the pump around to twist on the fitting.  Make sure you have adjusted the opening on the pump intake. I use full flow It's loud water flow when pumping through the fountain. Also fast moving which will keep it from freezing, Once you've done that untwist the wire tie on the power cord and place the pump inside the fountain its hard to do, so put it as far as you need to in order for it to stand up. Now place the cord out the access door Don't plug in the pump yet.
Get several 2.5 gallon buckets or a hose. Fill the bottom pool of the fountain until it is not draining into the fountain. That will be over the pump then keep hose nearby or one bucket of water nearby. Have your helper plug in the pump, as the water level in the bottom pool lowers fill it back up with the hose or bucket you have nearby.
Decorate and enjoy.

The tree itself is sturdy. It has a nice solid base,  a heavy duty ground stake, and 4 base stakes to stay in place. I also love that it fits in a slim box for storage.

product_name: 58 in. Tall Outdoor 8-Tier Rainforest Rock Water Fountain with LED Lights
review_title: Superb design; very realistic; eye and ear appeal
review_text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] The hardest part about setting up Alpine Corporation’s 8-Tier Rainforest Rock Water Fountain with LED Lights is deciding where to place it for maximum enjoyment.  I added it to our rose garden where it immediately catches the eye of visiting friends and where it provides looking and listening pleasure as we relax on the front deck.
The design is stunning, with each “rock” carefully and realistically molded and placed so that the water falls smoothly from one level to the next with no overspray, which minimizes evaporation and wasted water.  The lights are well placed for a soft underwater glow, and replacements are available through Alpine Corporation.  
Setup requires merely a level, a pair of scissors to cut zipties to unwrap the pump and light cords, a hose to fill the lower chamber at the back, and suitable electrical connections.  We have GFI outlets on our covered deck and started with an in-ground outlet timer, but since we keep it running 24/7, we switched to a 25-foot 12-gauge 15-amp heavy duty 3-outlet outdoor power cord.  2 outlets are needed – one for the pump and one for the lights.
When unpacking the fountain, I kept stopping to admire it and almost didn’t examine the molded foam packaging surrounding and protecting the fountain which contains 3 items – the sliding door that closes the back opening, the box containing the pump, and the instruction/warranty paperwork.
After unwrapping the pump cord and attaching the pump to the interior tubing that carries the water through the fountain, I placed it on the floor inside the fountain.  Unwrapping the light cord and leading it outside the fountain took just a second.  I then filled the base with water, and plugged in the fountain and the light cord.  The pump started circulating water through the fountain, and I added more water to the base, then slid the cover on the back opening.  Setup is that quick and easy, and I just check it every 4 to 5 days to see if a little more water should be added.
This is a beautiful water enhancement for any yard or garden or deck.

review_title: So I read some of the reviews prior to ordering and I was a little hesitant to purchase. People w...
review_text: So I read some of the reviews prior to ordering and I was a little hesitant to purchase. People wrote about the pump failing within weeks, paint bubbling in the water bowls, water not coming out of the cigar, missing lights...on and on. Bottom line is that Home Depot had a great price and it was worth taking a shot and purchasing. As for me, this unit works fine and looks great. I’ve been running mine for a while now. No pump failure and no bubbling paint. Folks, if the pump fails, it’s easily replaced with a fish tank pump. Not rocket science. One reviewer recommended clear coating the bowls to avoid the bubbling paint. I contend that some clear coat paints are very strong and may have actually compromised the paint...thus the bubbling. The manufacturer offers two of their products to maintain the fountain. I’ll be using those. As for my fountain, it arrived undamaged. All the parts were in the box. I had it hooked up and running in about 10 minutes. I did find a hose just lying on the bottom of the water reservoir and I did not know where it belonged as the fountain was filling and draining properly. The next day I took a real good look inside the unit and realized the tube directed water to the tongue of the middle bowl. I reconnected the hose to the connection points and it worked great. Some have talked about leaks. I would say the major ones were likely caused by the shipment process. Mine does not leak but, again, if you look inside the unit, you can see some really thin areas in the resin material.  Silicone will be a perfect fix if a leak developes. Plus, I would imagine that most are using this outdoors where a small leak is not going to damage anything. Evaporation will likely be more responsible for missing water rather than a leak. So my quality rating is really based on the fact that the resin could have been thicker in some areas to avoid any of these leaks. The LED lights are really the weakest part of the fountain. They work fine but do very little. They illuminate the faces faintly at night. They are mounted to the bottom of the water bowls and do illuminate the water but you have to be looking down at the water to really appreciate the illumination. I am happy with the purchase and it looks great. It really complements my outdoor tiki bar.

review_text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] Alpine's 54" Indoor/Outdoor Waterfall Rock Fountain with LED lights is the ultimate in spectacular easy-care fountains no matter where you choose to place it. 
There is no overspray, so all the water stays inside the fountain and tiers, important if you decide to set it up inside.  
After calculating the weight of the fountain plus the water when it is full, we knew our floors were strong enough.  After pondering which room and which location, we suddenly realized our small dogs would assume it to be the most amazing dog water fountain they'd ever seen.  We moved it outside to our entertainment area in the yard where we enjoy informal gatherings of family, friends, and neighbors, to provide a relaxing counterpoint to the conversational flow.
Unboxing is quick.  Look at the Styrofoam to find the cover for the back opening, the box containing the pump, and the instructions/warranty paperwork.  Choosing our location, we set it in place and gently moved it around for just the right viewing angle, leveled it, and pulled the connecting plugs for the pump and lights out of the lower back opening.
Since we have GFI outlets, the only other items needed were a water hose and the 25-foot 12-gauge 15-amp heavy duty 3-outlet outdoor power cord we chose for safety.  You need 2 outlets, one for the pump and one for the lights.  Filling the back opening, I then plugged in the pump and lights, waited for the water to circulate, and added more water.  The water flow is adjustable at the pump to evoke the flowing-water sound that is most pleasing to me, the listener.  Replacement lights and protective covers are available from Alpine Corporation.  
Whether curling up and unwinding by myself with a good book, working in the garden, or hosting a fun get-together, this fountain is pure joy.

review_text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] This is something I never knew I wanted to have, but I’m really happy to have gotten it! However, The sound can definitely be relaxing, and it's a kitten to an aquarium/ fountain. 
Overall, if you're looking something unique that your guests will definitely talk about, I highly recommend this!

review_text:
The pictures on the websites make this pump look small, and not produce a strong stream. That certainly is not true with the Eco-Twist Pump (by Alpine Corporation). This pump is a hefty-pump and is capable of transferring 88- gallons of water a minute. Be sure to follow instructions and use a two-inch pipe to get full use of the pump’s capability.

The Alpine Corporation is not an overseas company but is a U.S. manufacturer who has been producing products since 1999 in California. Warranty and replacement parts come from California.

review_text: Had an old bowl type cast concrete fountain-heavy, hard to replace pump, much maintenance.  Fiberglass fountains are the way to go-much easier to handle.
